candidate.name: causal simultaneous-profile Thorpe overturn state
candidate.scientific_question: Can density-profile reordering distinguish normal vertical mixing/stratification state from station-layer anomaly opportunity without using labels?

primary_source.title: Probability density of displacement and overturning length scales under diverse stratification
primary_source.supported_claim: Thorpe displacement is obtained by reordering a measured vertical profile to a stable monotonic profile; RMS displacement summarizes overturn scale.
primary_source.claim_boundary: The source studies resolved stratified profiles and turbulence. It does not validate sparse fixed P1 layers, station-layer anomaly precision, or transport.

physical_consistency.overlap: v21 already determined that an EOS/density transform adds no observation beyond existing temp/psal/depth physical-consistency features and the P2 TEOS/profile family.

stratification_peer_gate.overlap: Existing P1 code constructs label-blind simultaneous peer spread, gradient, and coherence features to distinguish mixed and stratified states.

vertical_rank.overlap: The executed vertical bracket/rank family already acts on layer ordering. Thorpe sorting is a physics-labeled rank displacement over the same simultaneous vertical order.

semantic_reconstructibility_audit.scientific_limitation: Temperature-only overturns can be salinity-compensated; a density implementation therefore inherits the already-closed EOS/TEOS family rather than defining a new observation axis.

decision.reason: The observable is structurally available only at S-ORS, the same station driving repeated identity collapse, and its density/rank ingredients are reconstructible from closed families.

next_research_gap: The original schema lacks a cross-station vertical scientific-state observable: G-ORS is single-layer and I-ORS has at most two simultaneous finite levels. A future nonduplicate axis needs an independently observed cross-station state covariate or an organizer-authorized external physical driver; neither is present in the train-only schema.
